parsed.explanation: The whole finiteness/large-prime-erasure content sits in the Lemma "For every sequence term x, the set σ(x) is good", whose proof reads only "Induction over the sequence terms in increasing order (standard; details omitted)." That is no argument. Elsewhere the text offers only a hypothesis-testing remark that "The construction Rp^k repairs this boundary issue" (no definition of R, no proof Rp^k is a term or lies in [A,x)), plus explicitly non-probative numerics ("These computations only test the lemma"). Since (3), (4) and hence periodicity all rest on this lemma, L6.2 is not established as written; supplying the omitted lemma proof is the minimal repair.
